inline.s: In this instruction Master Shandao states it most clearly:
single-minded
invocation of the Name — this is what conforms to the Buddha's original vow.
Yet Master Hōnen took the most crucial
“single-minded”

and cut off both words, altering it into: “invoking the Buddha-name is itself conforming to the Buddha's original vow,” and so reached the absurd conclusion that “invoking the name surely brings rebirth,” declaring loudly that “invocation surely assures rebirth”! Read this Words of the Dharma side by side with
Master Shandao's Pure Land Teachings
, and
you will plainly see how Master Hōnen tampered with Master Shandao's teaching to establish the school of the original vow
. For eight hundred years, who knows how many practitioners of Buddha-recitation it has misled, harming their lives of wisdom!

Q: Why must one have right mindfulness at the moment of death (the ten recollections continuing at death) to attain rebirth? Amitābha Buddha's five kalpas of reflection and measureless kalpas of practice — his entire great vow is to save every sentient being. With such a great compassionate heart, would he not, at the moment of our death, display his spiritual power and vow-force to receive and guide us?
A:

At the moment of death of every sentient being, Amitābha Buddha is receiving and guiding. It is only that sentient beings without right mindfulness at the moment of death cannot see it, and so follow their own deluded thoughts and, in accord with their karma, go to be reborn elsewhere.
So one must have right mindfulness at the moment of death in order to see Amitābha Buddha come to receive and guide, and to follow the Buddha to rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
On this principle, Master Zhongfeng, honored as the ancient Buddha of the south of the Yangtze, instructs in his The Three Periods of Mind-Connection:
“Although it is said that Amitābha takes hold of sentient beings and brings them to rebirth, one must believe
that it is only manifesting in accord with one's own mind
the mutual response of mind and way
, and in the end
(after all)
is not obtained from outside

[It is only manifesting in accord with one's own mind] Amitābha Buddha, coming to receive (take hold of) sentient beings, manifests only in accord with one's own mind — this is due to the mutual response of mind and way, and is not obtained from outside. So only one with right mindfulness at death can see the Buddha come, while the others around do not see it.

For those dying sentient beings who lack right mindfulness at death, since there is no responsive stimulus, naturally Amitābha Buddha's receiving does not manifest in their minds, and so they too do not see the Buddha come — not that Amitābha Buddha did not come to receive them.
So whether or not one attains rebirth depends entirely on whether one has right mindfulness at death
(the ten recollections continuing at death)
This is why
Master Shandao, the incarnation of Amitābha Buddha, and Master Yongming, also an incarnation of Amitābha Buddha, both earnestly instruct:
to accomplish the ten recollections continuing at death
(see
The Conditions for Rebirth
. This is the Buddha's own teaching!
[Mutual response of mind and way] The response of sentient beings and the response of Amitābha Buddha interpenetrate.

On the principle of mind and way mutually responding at the moment of death, Master Yinguang, the incarnation of Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva, instructs in the Preface to the Guide to Pure Land Practice for Beginners:

“The minds of sentient beings are like water, and Amitābha Buddha is like the moon. When sentient beings are complete in faith and vow and with utmost sincerity move the Buddha, then the Buddha responds — as when the water is clear, the moon appears. If the mind is not pure, not sincere, is in accord with greed, anger, and delusion, and runs counter to the Buddha, it is like turbid, stirred water, and although the moon does not fail to shine upon it, it cannot be clearly reflected.”

Vernacular: The minds of sentient beings are like water, and Amitābha Buddha is like the moon. When sentient beings are complete in faith and vow and with utmost sincerity move the Buddha, then the Buddha responds — as when the water is clear and still, the moon appears (a metaphor for the pure mind of right mindfulness manifesting the receiving of Amitābha Buddha). If the mind is not pure, not sincere, is in accord with greed, anger, and delusion, and runs counter to the Buddha, it is like turbid, stirred water; although the Buddha-moon does not fail to shine upon it (a metaphor that Amitābha Buddha is always receiving every dying sentient being), yet it cannot be clearly reflected (a metaphor that a stirred, turbid, disordered mind cannot manifest the receiving of Amitābha Buddha,
but instead follows its own deluded thoughts and, in accord with its karma, goes to be reborn elsewhere

“Only when the water is clear and still does it appear; when the water is turbid and stirred it hides. The moon is certainly without accepting and rejecting; that it does not appear is because the water is murky and churning, having no way to receive its reflection.”

Vernacular: Only when the water is clear and still does the moon's reflection appear; when the water is turbid and stirred, the reflection does not appear. The moon certainly shines without accepting and rejecting; that it does not appear is because the water is murky and churning, with no way to receive its reflection. (Metaphor: only those sentient beings with right mindfulness at death can see the receiving of Amitābha Buddha, while those without right mindfulness at death cannot see the receiving of Amitābha Buddha. Amitābha Buddha certainly receives every dying sentient being without accepting or rejecting; that those without right mindfulness at death cannot see his receiving is because
their own minds are murky
and disordered,
and so
they follow their own deluded thoughts and, in accord with their karma, go to be reborn elsewhere

So for the practitioner of Buddha-recitation, single-minded right mindfulness at the moment of death is extremely important. One who recites a thousand times, ten thousand times, even all day and all year — does so for nothing other than to make this single thought of recitation familiar,
to ensure that at the moment of death this thought continues without break, and that it manifests the receiving of Amitābha Buddha
. Therefore Master Shandao, the incarnation of Amitābha Buddha, and Master Yongming, also an incarnation of Amitābha Buddha, both earnestly instruct:
to accomplish the ten recollections continuing at death
(see
The Conditions for Rebirth
This is the measure of holy speech! If one does not listen to the words of Amitābha Buddha, whose words will one listen to?

[Continuing (xiāng xù)] The thought of recitation follows on without break, unmingled with deluded thoughts. [Measure of holy speech] This is what the sages have spoken — correct and without error, certainly to be received in faith.
